te: Now listen carefully.
en: Now listen carefully.

te: This may be the single most important rule in Indian health insurance.
en: This may be the single most important rule in Indian health insurance.

te: It is called the moratorium period.
en: It is called the moratorium period.

te: Earlier, this period was eight years.
en: Earlier, this period was eight years.

te: But in twenty twenty-four, the I-R-D-A-I brought it down from eight years to five years.
en: But in twenty twenty-four, the I-R-D-A-I brought it down from eight years to five years.

te: That means sixty continuous months in a row, with no break in your policy.
en: That means sixty continuous months in a row, with no break in your policy.

te: So, what does it mean for you?
en: So, what does it mean for you?

te: After five years of continuous cover, the insurance company legally CANNOT question your policy or your claim on grounds of non-disclosure, like an old disease you did not mention.
en: After five years of continuous cover, the insurance company legally CANNOT question your policy or your claim on grounds of non-disclosure, like an old disease you did not mention.

te: Read that again.
en: Read that again.

te: After five years, an old health history cannot be used as an excuse.
en: After five years, an old health history cannot be used as an excuse.

te: There is only one single exception.
en: There is only one single exception.

te: Proven fraud that the company has to establish.
en: Proven fraud that the company has to establish.

te: Not a forgotten fever, not an undiagnosed ache... active, deliberate fraud.
en: Not a forgotten fever, not an undiagnosed ache... active, deliberate fraud.

te: Your normal policy limits and exclusions still apply, and if you port your policy to another insurer, your years move with you.
en: Your normal policy limits and exclusions still apply, and if you port your policy to another insurer, your years move with you.

te: If you cancel and buy a new one, the count resets to zero.
en: If you cancel and buy a new one, the count resets to zero.

te: Now think about our family at the billing counter.
en: Now think about our family at the billing counter.

te: Six years of continuous policy.
en: Six years of continuous policy.

te: A letter that says non-disclosure.
en: A letter that says non-disclosure.

te: That excuse directly violates the I-R-D-A-I rule.
en: That excuse directly violates the I-R-D-A-I rule.

te: And there is one more rule... a clock.
en: And there is one more rule... a clock.

te: When the hospital sends the final discharge request to the insurance company, the company must give final approval within three hours.
en: When the hospital sends the final discharge request to the insurance company, the company must give final approval within three hours.

te: I-R-D-A-I mandates that the patient should not be made to wait.
en: I-R-D-A-I mandates that the patient should not be made to wait.

te: If the approval comes later than three hours, any extra amount the hospital charges for that delay is paid by the insurance company from its own funds... not by you.
en: If the approval comes later than three hours, any extra amount the hospital charges for that delay is paid by the insurance company from its own funds... not by you.

te: Remember this rule, and ask for it at the discharge counter.
en: Remember this rule, and ask for it at the discharge counter.
